chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man leaves behind for his family three thousand dirhams as expenses for two years. Is Zakat due upon it?' He said, 'If he was present, then Zakat is due upon it, and if he was absent, then there is nothing in it.'
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on money left for family expenses if the owner is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that Zakat liability on funds reserved for family maintenance depends on the owner's presence and control; if he is present, Zakat is due, but if absent, it is exempt. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that effective possession (qabd) and the ability to utilize the wealth are key determinants for Zakat obligations. It provides practical guidance for families managing household funds when the breadwinner is traveling or away.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘The man leaves behind three thousand Dirhams as expense monies (with his wife) for two years. Would there be Zakāt upon it?’
Heasws said: ‘If he was present, so upon her would be the Zakāt, but if he was absent, so there is nothing with regards to it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from Sama‘ah from abu Basir who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who leaves with his family three thousand dirham for the expenses of two years is there Zakat on it? He (the Imam) said, ‘If he is present, Zakat is due, but if he is absent, Zakat is not due.’”
